select.what: The Fail2Ban jail this page shows and changes, for example sshd for SSH logins.
select.who: Anyone reading bans; admins pick the jail before they change settings, the whitelist or ban an address.
select.effect: Only switches the view. The banned list, whitelist, settings and the manual ban form all work on the selected jail.

bantime.what: How long an address stays banned, in seconds. -1 bans it for good.
bantime.who: Admins deciding how hard repeated failed logins are punished.
bantime.effect: Saving applies it to the running jail at once; an empty field leaves it unchanged. The panel does not check the value: Fail2Ban refuses an invalid one and the save reports it. It is not written to Fail2Ban's config files. A long time also keeps you out longer if your own address gets banned.

maxretry.what: How many failures within the find time trigger a ban.
maxretry.who: Admins balancing protection against users who mistype their password.
maxretry.effect: Applied to the running jail at once, not to the config files. A low number bans attackers sooner but can also ban you; add your own address to the whitelist first.

findtime.what: The time window, in seconds, in which failures are counted toward the maximum.
findtime.who: Admins tuning how slow attacks are caught.
findtime.effect: Applied to the running jail at once, not to the config files. A longer window counts more failures together, so it bans more often, including legitimate users.

ip.what: An IP address or a CIDR range this jail never bans (Fail2Ban's ignoreip).
ip.who: Admins who want to keep their own office or home address, or a monitoring server, from being locked out.
ip.effect: Only admins can add it. The server accepts one IP or a CIDR range and refuses anything else. It is added to the running jail only, not to the config files. A wide range also protects attackers inside it.

ip.what: One IPv4 or IPv6 address to ban by hand. Ranges (CIDR) are refused; a permanent ban with the iptables engine takes IPv4 only.
ip.who: Admins blocking an address they already know is attacking.
ip.effect: Without "permanent", Fail2Ban bans it in the selected jail. Nothing stops you from banning your own address this way, so check it before you confirm.

jail.what: The jail the temporary ban goes into. It is the same choice as the jail selector at the top of the page.
jail.who: Admins choosing which service the address is banned from.
jail.effect: Changing it also switches the page to that jail. A permanent ban ignores the jail.

permanent.what: Blocks the address in the server firewall instead of a Fail2Ban jail.
permanent.who: Admins who want an attacker kept out until someone removes the block.
permanent.effect: The block stays until it is removed on the Permanent bans tab. With the nftables firewall engine the server refuses a block that would cut off your current session; with the legacy iptables firewall there is no such check.
